title: Vaccine-Associated Measles Encephalitis in Immunocompromised Child, California, USA.
ehr_evidence: The study was a single-patient case report; data were derived from clinical notes, a nasopharyngeal swab, MRI/PET imaging, and formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) brain tissue analyzed by histopathology and metagenomic RNA sequencing—not from any electronic or computerized health-record database.
summary: A case report of a fatal vaccine-associated measles encephalitis caused by the Edmonston-Enders vaccine strain in an immunocompromised infant with acute myeloid leukemia in California, USA, confirmed by whole-genome RNA sequencing of measles virus from brain tissue.
key_findings: 38.0% (68/179) of uracil-containing codons in the matrix (M) gene contained >1 uracil-to-cytosine mutation at levels ≥5%, indicating biased M-gene hypermutation consistent with persistent CNS measles virus infection.

Metagenomic RNA sequencing of brain tissue acquired 50.7 million reads, of which 190,303 aligned to the Edmonston-Enders (Moraten) vaccine measles virus, yielding 500× coverage over 98.2% of the genome (mean coverage 1,540×).
No known hyperfusogenic fusion gene mutations were identified.
The patient died despite treatment with intravenous ribavirin, intrathecal interferon-α, and inosine pranobex; the family declined autopsy.
captured_features: Whole-genome RNA sequencing of measles virus from FFPE brain tissue
Matrix (M) gene hypermutation (U-to-C mutations at ≥5% allele frequency)
Histopathology (H&E and GFAP immunoperoxidase staining) showing astrogliosis without inflammation, neoplastic cells, or definite inclusions
MRI abnormal signals and PET hyperperfusion of the insula and thalamus
Nasopharyngeal swab positive for MV RNA by multiplex RT-PCR
Clinical course of acute myeloid leukemia and stem cell transplant
pathologies_diseases: Vaccine-associated measles encephalitis (measles inclusion body encephalitis)
population: A single immunocompromised infant/child (1-year-old) in California, USA, with acute myeloid leukemia
limitations: Single case report (n=1) with no autopsy (family declined), limiting generalizability and causal inference.
